mutants.reason: The memory write enable is inverted, so accepted writes are not stored and rejected cycles overwrite entries. Data read back is wrong.
The REL flush check uses OR instead of AND. Because rd_ptr is already 0, the write FSM leaves REL while the acknowledge is still 1, so o_sw_rst_busy falls earlier than it should.
The read block term is inverted. Reads are blocked in normal RUN and allowed during a software reset, so o_empty, o_empty_thr and read acceptance are wrong.
The RUN-to-REQ condition becomes AND. A low i_rst_n_sw alone no longer starts the software reset sequence, because pend is 0 in RUN.
The hardware reset value of o_overflow becomes 1, so o_overflow is high while i_rst_n_wr is low.

The read FSM can only be in ACK after req_view was 1. req stays 1 from REQ through HOLD, and the write pointer is cleared in PTR, before req falls in REL. Writes stay blocked until the write FSM returns to RUN, and that needs ack=0, which means the read FSM has already left ACK. So whenever req_view=0 in ACK, wr_ptr_view is already 0 and the `|| (wr_ptr_view=='0)` change cannot alter any transition.
The empty flop gets the inverted occupancy comparison, so o_empty is 1 when the FIFO has data and 0 when it is empty.
The read pointer advances when no read is accepted and holds when one is accepted. Read data order and occupancy are wrong.
The reset value of o_empty_thr becomes 0 instead of 1 during hardware reset.
The reset value of o_underflow becomes 1, so o_underflow is high while i_rst_n_rd is low.
o_sw_rst_busy is inverted. It is 1 in normal RUN and 0 during a software reset.
The request to the read side is inverted for the REQ state. The read side sees a wrong request, so the sequence and the read blocking and flush are wrong.
The write pointer advances when no write is accepted and holds when one is accepted. Occupancy, o_full and the data placement are wrong.
The reset value of o_full_thr becomes 1 instead of 0 during hardware reset.
The read pointer wrap condition is inverted. The pointer resets to 0 at almost every step, so the read order and o_empty are wrong.
The read pointer is cleared in every state except RST. It is cleared constantly in normal operation and not cleared in RST during a software reset.
The reset value of o_empty becomes 0, so o_empty is low during hardware reset.
The acknowledge resets to 1 instead of 0. A software reset requested while the read reset is still asserted is acknowledged at once, which changes the o_sw_rst_busy timing.
The write pointer wrap condition is inverted. The pointer resets to 0 at almost every step, so occupancy, o_full and the data order are wrong.
The REL flush condition is negated. The FSM leaves REL when the acknowledge or read pointer is not clear, and stays in REL after the flush completes. o_sw_rst_busy never falls at the right time.
The reset value of o_full becomes 1 during hardware reset.
The read FSM waits in ACK for a non-zero write pointer, which is 0. It never returns to RUN, so ack stays 1, the software reset never completes and reads stay blocked.
The RUN to RST transition is inverted. The read FSM leaves RUN when there is no request and stays when there is one, so the sequence is not acknowledged.
The request term for the HOLD state is inverted, so reg_req is 1 in RUN, REQ, PTR and REL and 0 in HOLD. The read side is blocked in normal operation and the flush behaviour changes.
HOLD is left when i_rst_n_sw is low instead of high. The sequence ends while the request is still asserted and holds after it is released.
The reset value of o_sw_rst_busy becomes 1, so busy is high while i_rst_n_wr is low.
The acknowledge is inverted. It is 1 in RUN and 0 in ACK, so the handshake with the write side fails and the software reset sequence is wrong.
The ACK exit condition is negated. The read FSM leaves ACK while the request is still high and stays in ACK after the flush is clear.
The request term for the PTR state is inverted, so reg_req is 1 in RUN, REQ, HOLD and REL and 0 in PTR. The read side is blocked in normal operation and the handshake is wrong.
The REQ state advances on ack=0 instead of ack=1. The write FSM moves on before the read side acknowledges and the sequence is wrong.

reg_sw_rst_req_d is only read through w_sw_rst_fall, and that only matters in the REQ and PTR states. After hardware reset the FSM is in RUN and its first clock edge reloads req_d with ~i_rst_n_sw. So the reset value is never used.
The read pointer is cleared in every state except RST. It is cleared constantly in normal operation and not cleared during a software reset.
The reset condition of the read FSM block is inverted. The state and acknowledge are reset on every clock edge when reset is not asserted and run freely when it is.
The REL flush check requires rd_ptr_view to be non-zero, but rd_ptr is 0 after the reset. The write FSM never returns to RUN and o_sw_rst_busy stays 1.
The reset condition of the write FSM block is inverted. The FSM, busy, req and pend flops are reset on every clock edge when reset is not asserted, and the software reset never runs.
reg_sw_rst_pend resets to 1, so after hardware reset RUN sees a pending request and starts a software reset sequence on its own. o_sw_rst_busy rises with no i_rst_n_sw request.
